title: Animal, fungus, or neither?
question: What sets an animal apart from plants and fungi?
hook: Plants, fungi and animals all have many cells and all use oxygen, so what really marks a creature as an animal?
idea: Animals take in and digest food inside their bodies, and their cells sit in a flexible framework instead of rigid walls.

beats.prompt: You find a new multicellular organism that uses oxygen and cannot make its own food. Which extra clue would best tell you it is an animal and not a fungus?

choices.label: Its cells are held in a flexible framework rather than in cell walls
It breathes oxygen
choices.feedback: It tempts because animals do breathe oxygen, but plants and fungi are aerobic too.

choices.label: It is made of many cells
choices.feedback: Animals are multicellular, but so are plants and fungi.

choices.label: It cannot produce its own food
choices.feedback: Animals share this with fungi, so it cannot separate the two.

beats.explain: Animals, plants and fungi are all eukaryotic, multicellular and aerobic, and fungi cannot make their own food either. Animal cells sit in an extracellular matrix, while the cells of plants, algae and fungi are held by cell walls.

beats.prompt: Sort each feature by whether animals share it with plants and fungi or whether it sets animals apart.
items: A hollow ball of cells in early development
Spontaneous body movement at some life stage
Cells surrounded by an extracellular matrix
beats.explain: Being eukaryotic, multicellular and aerobic is common to animals, plants and fungi. Motility, a blastula stage and cells in an extracellular matrix set animals apart.

beats.prompt: Put the early steps of animal sexual reproduction and development in order.
items: Sperm and egg fuse into a zygote
The zygote divides into a hollow blastula
The blastula folds in to form a gastrula
The germ layers differentiate into tissues and organs
beats.explain: Gametes fuse to form zygotes, which develop into a blastula. In most groups that folds into a gastrula, and its germ layers then differentiate into tissues and organs.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: Animals cannot produce their own food.
Fungi cannot produce their own food either.
So any organism that cannot make its own food must be an animal.
beats.explain: Animals share that trait with fungi, so it cannot define an animal. Animals differ in other ways, such as holding their cells in an extracellular matrix instead of cell walls.
